name: Muhammad Moosa Raza
affiliation: M.Sc. Ecology & Nature Management, RUDN University
tagline: Remote sensing for floods, drought and land-system change — with a working obsession for when these methods quietly fail

availability.detail: Open to positions in remote sensing, hydrology, land-system science and climate risk. Happy to discuss how my work could extend a group's existing research.

about: I build satellite-based environmental measurements, then try to break them. Across nine open studies over Pakistan, the recurring result is that the textbook method returns a confident number that does not survive scrutiny.
I want a PhD where that becomes the research question: how we establish an Earth observation measurement is trustworthy before it drives a flood warning, a drought declaration or a carbon budget.

methodsAudit.lede: Four times a standard method gave a confident answer that did not hold up. Each was caught by testing the method against itself.

items.note: Gamma has zero density at zero, but 53.7% of pixel-months here are rainless. A 95% false-alarm rate on the most severe category.
Compositing a multi-week window understated the true peak threefold by averaging the flood away.
Control years give +0.076. Almost the entire raw signal was ordinary double-cropping, not flood response.
A predictor silently doing nothing. Caught only because a feature-importance plot looked wrong.

approach.title: Validate against time
approach.description: Chronological holdout, so a model never sees the events it is scored on.

approach.title: Cross-check the sensor
approach.description: Radar against optical, retrieval against reanalysis. Independent agreement beats one high score.

approach.title: Report what does not flatter
approach.description: Lead with the number that undercuts the result, then show what still holds.

approach.title: Ship code and caveats
approach.description: Every study public, with training data and a written account of its limits.

bullets: Designed and published nine end-to-end EO studies over Pakistan covering flood mapping, flood susceptibility, drought, soil moisture, speckle filtering and crop mapping
Established a consistent methodological standard across all of them: chronological validation, independent cross-sensor checks, and explicit reporting of negative and null results

Identified and documented several failure modes in widely used workflows, including a silent Google Earth Engine distance-operator fault and a 95% false-alarm rate in textbook SPI over zero-inflated rainfall
Released every study as open code with training data, GIS exports and written limitations, so results can be reproduced and contested

experience.role: Master’s Thesis Researcher — Remote Sensing & Carbon Modelling
bullets: Designed a multi-decadal (1993–2023) LULC analysis pipeline using Landsat imagery in Google Earth Engine
Implemented Random Forest classification reaching 97.8%–99.2% accuracy, Kappa 0.971–0.989
Quantified urban expansion (+117%) and vegetation loss (−27,639 ha) across Lahore District
Estimated ecosystem carbon dynamics: a total loss of roughly 3.15 million metric tons
Integrated the InVEST carbon model as an independent check on the class-based estimate
Key contribution: showed how urban land transitions drive large-scale carbon loss in rapidly developing regions

Modelling & Analysis: Accuracy assessment (confusion matrix, Kappa, IoU, ROC)
